analysis.evidence: The preposition בְּ in בַּיַהְוֶה identifies YHWH as the one Abram trusted. Abram’s trust answers YHWH’s promise of offspring in the preceding verse.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ “and” precedes הֶאֱמִן, a Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular. Abram is the subject.

analysis.evidence: In וְהֶאֱמִן בַּיַהְוֶה, the preposition introduces the one whom Abram trusted, Yahweh.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בַּ means “in” and precedes the proper name יַהְוֶה.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: The suffix הָ points back to Abram’s act of trusting YHWH. לּוֹ identifies the person to whom it was credited, and צְדָקָה states what it counted as.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular. The third feminine singular object suffix הָ means “it.”
analysis.sense: reckon to, set to one's account, impute

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:6 as an example of the existing le-dative sense of Hebrew לְ.
draft.definition: To the person to whom something is given or credited.
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:6 uses לּוֹ with וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ to identify the recipient of the credit.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה, “he counted it to him as righteousness,” the suffix on the verb supplies “it,” while לּוֹ identifies Abram as the person to whom it was credited.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ takes the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix וֹ. The dagesh doubles the lamed in this context.
analysis.sense: Marks the person to whom something is credited.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה, “he reckoned it to him as righteousness,” the suffix ־הָ refers back to Abram’s believing Yahweh. צְדָקָה states what that trust was counted as.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew common noun, feminine singular, in the absolute state.
